# Volume 3 — Chapter XXXIV John Fairlie Speaks at Last

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Nell possessed a faint expectation that some result might yet emerge. However, none occurred. John Fairlie arrived to take Thora out in his carriage, and he accompanied her on foot from the prayer-meeting, continuing the routine he had pursued for twenty years, and one he appeared destined to maintain for another twenty. Summer drew to a close. Nell conducted her school, composed letters, and engaged in some study. Her journeys to and from the schoolhouse were enjoyable. She invariably traveled through the swamp; it formed a delightful spot—a marshy ground, verdant with the most vivid mossy mounds; a shimmering stream turned and twisted across it, and spruce trees grew straight, their branches draped with grayish-green moss, their roots covered with every variety of forest beauty.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0000 }

Even so, Nell considered her existence on Coombe Road to be somewhat dull. Of course, a single amusing event did occur.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0001 }

She had not laid eyes on the gangly, flaxen-haired Samuel who had brought the peppermints since the night he visited, except for occasional encounters along the path. However, on a humid night in August he showed up, quietly sitting down upon the wooden bench near the porch. He was dressed in his customary work clothes, which were made up of mended pants, a blue denim shirt that was frayed at the elbows, and a tattered hat made of straw. A straw was tucked in his mouth, which he continued to chew as he gazed seriously at Nell. Nell put down her book with a sigh and picked up her doily. Having a dialogue with Sam was truly impossible.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0002 }

Following an extended period of quiet, Sam abruptly broke the silence.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0003 }

“I am moving away from that place,” he stated suddenly, gesturing with his straw toward the adjacent home.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0004 }

“Oh, do you happen to be?” Nell asked in a polite manner.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0005 }

“Yep.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0006 }

“And to what place are you heading at present?”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0007 }

“Well, I’ve given some thought to acquiring a spot for myself. A location that would fit my needs exists in Millersville. However, should I take the lease, having a wife will be necessary.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0008 }

“I guess that’s true,” Nell remarked absently.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0009 }

“Yep.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0010 }

A further extended period of silence ensued. At last, Sam took his straw out once more and remarked,
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0011 }

“Will yeh hev me?”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0012 }

“Wh—a—t!” Nell gasped.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0013 }

“Will yeh hev me?”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0014 }

“Are you suggesting—that I MARRY you?” asked miserable Nell weakly.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0015 }

“Yep.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0016 }

“Why, I’m barely acquainted with you,” cried Nell indignantly.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0017 }

“However, ye would become familiar with me once our wedding was over,” Sam said.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0018 }

Nell summoned what remained of her modest pride.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0019 }

“I will most definitely not marry you,” she stated with a haughty air.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0020 }

“Well, you could certainly do worse,” protested Sam. “I work hard, plus I have saved some money in the bank.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0021 }

“Never bring this up to me another time. What could have possibly planted that notion in your mind?” inquired Nell, as her anger was overcome by her amusement. The circumstance was utterly preposterous.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0022 }

“You seem like a promising girl, and you move along at a good pace,” Sam stated. “A lazy woman isn't what I'm looking for. Give it some thought. My opinion won't be changing anytime soon. Anyway, I need to head off. The cows need milking.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0023 }

Recent years had chipped away at Nell’s notions about marriage offers, leaving her with hardly any remaining. Consequently, this particular proposal amused her entirely, without causing her any underlying pain. Later that evening, she performed an imitation of unfortunate Sam for Thora, causing the two of them to indulge in uncontrolled laughter at his sudden burst of emotion.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0024 }

It was one afternoon, as Nell’s stay at Coombe Road was coming to an end, that Hector Ward drove in great hurry down to “Wayside” to fetch Thora.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0025 }

“They need you over at the Fairlie place right away,” he stated. “It’s my genuine belief that old Mrs. Fairlie is finally going to pass away, having feigned it for two decades.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0026 }

Thora darted off to retrieve her hat. Nell inquired whether Mrs. Fairlie was feeling worse than her normal state.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0027 }

“Her condition is far worse,” Hector declared gravely, “which leads me to believe it is grave. On previous occasions, she would scream and thrash about frantically. Right now, she just lies there without making a sound. You can be certain that whenever Mrs. Fairlie falls quiet, she is extremely ill.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0028 }

“Is old Mrs. Fairlie someone you dislike?” Nell inquired with curiosity.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0029 }

“I enjoy cats when they are cats. I do not enjoy cats when they are women,” Hector answered mysteriously.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0030 }

In the dusk, Thora returned to the house.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0031 }

“Mrs. Fairlie has passed away,” she stated with fatigue. “Her death occurred shortly following my arrival. Only a single time did she address me—‘I suppose you’ll marry John now?’ was what she remarked. Nell, that pierced me deeply. Imagine that his very own mother believed I refrained from marrying John on account of her! Nor was I able to utter anything in response—additional women were present. It was a relief to me that John had left.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0032 }

Thora started weeping dismally. However, Nell made her a warm beverage of ginger tea to console her. Indeed, Nell realized afterward that white pepper had been used by her rather than ginger; nevertheless, the distinction was never known by Thora.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0033 }

When the sun was setting on the evening following the funeral, Thora and Nell sat together upon the steps of the front porch. Within the pinelands, the wind had grown still, while vivid flashes of heat-lightning pulsed over the skies to the north. Wearing her unattractive black dress, Thora appeared at her absolute worst, her eyes and nose showing red from her tears. Few words passed between them, as Thora appeared slightly to begrudge the attempts Nell made to comfort her. It was clear she favored remaining unhappy.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0034 }

Without warning, the latch on the gate clicked, and John Fairlie marched into the garden. Crossing directly over the bed of geraniums, he moved in their direction. Thora rose to her feet. Nell did as well. A tall girl, Nell was dressed in white; yet John Fairlie took no notice of her.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0035 }

“Thora,” he asked, “would you become my wife?”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0036 }

Those statements erupted as though twenty years of eager suppression forced them to be voiced instantly, prior to all else.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0037 }

Because Thora’s face was already as red as it could possibly get from weeping, it became an exceedingly unattractive shade of purple instead.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0038 }

“How come you failed to inquire earlier?” she asked deliberately.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0039 }

“I was unable to. She extracted a vow from me against it—mother extracted a vow from me against it. Nineteen years back, a dreadful illness seized her. We believed she would not survive it. She begged me for a vow that I would not request your hand in marriage during her lifetime. I was unwilling to make such a vow, even with our shared belief that her remaining time was brief—the doctor assigned her a mere six months. Yet she pleaded for it upon her knees, ill and in pain. I was forced to give my word.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0040 }

“What reason did your mother have to dislike me?” Thora exclaimed.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0041 }

“It is nothing—absolutely nothing. She simply refused to have a different woman—whichever woman it might be—present during her lifetime. She claimed that without my vow, her death would occur instantly, making me her murderer. Consequently, I gave my word. Ever since, she has bound me to that pledge, despite my own moments of falling to my knees to plead for my release.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0042 }

“Why was I not told about this?” Thora inquired with a choke. “If I had merely been aware! Why did you not simply let me know?”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0043 }

“I gave her my word that I would keep it completely secret,” John uttered in a raspy voice. “She had me swear upon the Holy Book; Thora, had I imagined it would last for such a lengthy time, I would have refused. You cannot comprehend the agony I have endured throughout these nineteen years, Thora. It is clear to me that I caused you pain as well, yet you will still become my wife, won't you, Thora? Please, Thora, will you not? As quickly as possible, I arrived to seek your hand.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0044 }

In that instance, the dazed Nell regained her composure, recognizing that her presence there was inappropriate. Sneaking off, she avoided seeing Thora until the following morning, at which time Thora recounted the remainder of the tale to her.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0045 }

“That old woman is deceitful, relentless, and cruel!” Nell cried.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0046 }

“Be quiet—she has passed away,” Thora stated gravely. “If that weren't the case—however it is. Therefore we are forbidden to talk ill of her. All the same, I have finally found joy, Nell. And I would not have cared about enduring such a lengthy wait in the least had I merely understood the reason.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0047 }

“When is your wedding to take place?”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0048 }

“In the coming month. Naturally, it is going to be extremely muted. I imagine folk are going to gossip dreadful. It will be said by them that I rushed to grab John the moment his unfortunate mother was no longer around. John wished to inform them of what actually happened, however I uttered, ‘No, John; after all she was your mother, and we’ll keep the secret between us, and not cast any shadow on her memory. I don’t mind what people say, now that I know the truth myself. It don’t matter a mite. Let it all be buried with the dead’ says I to him. Therefore I persuaded him to concur with my view.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0049 }

“I could never be nearly as forgiving as you are,” Nell remarked, in a somewhat irritated manner.
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0050 }

“Your perspective on numerous matters will change once you reach my age,” Thora remarked with tolerance. “Learning how to forgive is among the lessons age brings us. Doing so is simpler at forty than it was at twenty.”
{: #nw-v03-c34-p0051 }
